sections.html:
Richland owners generally pick from three paths: a traditional listing, a sale handled without an agent, or a cash buyer who takes the house as it is. Cash tends to be fastest because no lender must approve the buyer. Title work and your own paperwork still set the closing day.

Richland is in Benton County, part of the Tri-Cities in southeastern Washington. Prices run well under Seattle-area levels, and the city has been gaining people, from 60,580 in the April 2020 estimates base to 65,258 on July 1, 2025, a rise of 7.7 percent.

  • List when the house is ready to show and a wait for the buyer's loan is acceptable.
  • Choose cash for an inherited house, a rental with tenants, a place that needs work, or a firm move date.
  • Sell by owner if you can manage the contract, the seller disclosure form and the county excise tax affidavit.

Ask each bidder to put price, closing date and the closing cost split in writing so you can weigh them fairly.

These numbers describe the city as a whole, not one neighborhood.

Housing measureRichland
Median value of owner-occupied homes, 2020 to 2024$436,700
Owner-occupied housing rate, 2020 to 202464.4%
Median gross rent, 2020 to 2024$1,468
Median household income, 2020 to 2024$95,813
Residents age 65 and over16.9%
Mean travel time to work20.4 minutes

A large older population points to a steady flow of downsizing and estate sales. A commute of 20.4 minutes is short, and it is a fair selling point to mention in your listing or to a buyer.

A good share of Richland's older housing dates to World War II. In 1943 the U.S. Army took over land along the Columbia River for the Manhattan Project, and the population jumped from about 300 to 25,000 by the end of the war. The Army planned the city and built prefabricated duplexes and single-family homes in many floor plans identified by letter, which is why they are called alphabet houses. The government owned the homes until the 1950s, and the last government-owned home was sold on May 16, 1960.

If yours is one of these houses, expect buyers to ask about the roof, wiring, insulation and any additions. The Gold Coast Historic District in north Richland, made up of houses from the Cold War expansion, was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 2005, so check the status of a property in that area before you plan changes.

Richland is semi-arid, with hot summers, about 7 inches of precipitation a year, and a 118 degree high during the 2021 heat wave. Inspectors tend to ask about the air conditioner's age, attic insulation, roof condition and the irrigation system. Lawns and landscaping here usually rely on irrigation water, which affects both the tax bill and the disclosure paperwork covered below.

sections.h2: Benton County property tax at sale
sections.html:
The Benton County Treasurer collects tax for the county, cities, school districts and other taxing districts, and the bill follows the property. Bills are generally certified in mid to late January. The first half is late if unpaid after April 30, and the second half is late after October 31. A due date that lands on a weekend moves to the next Monday, and a payment counts as on time if postmarked by the due date.

On residential property with four or fewer units, RCW 84.56.020 sets interest at 9 percent a year on delinquent tax and bars additional penalties. The county will not foreclose until real property is a full three years delinquent. Statements go out only at the start of the year, based on who owned the property on December 1 of the prior year, so the closing is where you decide how the tax is handled. Have the title company confirm the balance before you sign.

Some Richland parcels also carry irrigation assessments collected on the tax bill. Benton Irrigation District, Columbia Irrigation District and Kiona Irrigation District bill through the Treasurer, while Kennewick Irrigation District must be paid directly to the district. Find out which one serves your address.

Owners aged 61 or older, or retired because of a disability, may qualify for a senior or disabled exemption, and deferral is also possible. Call the Benton County Assessor at (509) 735-2394 about those programs. Valuation appeals go to the Benton County Board of Equalization.

Every transfer of title in Benton County needs a Real Estate Excise Tax Affidavit filed with the deed. The Treasurer will not take the affidavit unless sections 1 through 7 are complete, and mobile homes need a separate affidavit. Forms are available online and at both Treasurer locations, 620 Market Street in Prosser and 7122 W Okanogan Place in Kennewick. The seller usually pays the tax, due on the date of sale, which the Department of Revenue treats as the date the deed is notarized.

For sales beginning January 1, 2027, the state rate is 1.1 percent up to $551,000, with a local rate added. Ask your escrow officer or the Benton County Treasurer for the local rate and for the brackets that apply if you close before the new year.

The seller disclosure statement under RCW 64.06.020 is due within five business days after contract acceptance, and the buyer has three business days after delivery to rescind. The form has sections on household water, irrigation water rights, sewer or on-site systems and wood-burning appliances, all common in Richland's mix of city and rural-edge lots. For permit history, the City of Richland issues building permits through its online permitting system, live since June 3, 2024, and its Building Division is at 625 Swift Boulevard.

sections.h2: Checklist before you accept an offer
sections.html:
Line up these items:

  • The deed, loan payoff figure and a current tax statement from the Benton County Treasurer.
  • Any irrigation district bill or water rights paperwork tied to the lot.
  • Permit records for additions, decks or finished basements.
  • A completed excise tax affidavit with sections 1 through 7 filled in.

In a cash sale the steps are short. You accept an offer, escrow opens, and the title company searches the record. Your loan is paid from the proceeds, you sign the deed before a notary, and the county receives the affidavit and tax. Funds are released after recording. There is no appraisal or lender review, which is why a cash sale can close on a date you choose.

faqs.q: How long does it take to sell a house in Richland, WA?
faqs.a: A cash sale can close as soon as title work is done, often on a date you set. A listing takes longer because of showings, inspections and the buyer's financing. Request the closing date in writing from any buyer.

faqs.q: When are Benton County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due by April 30 and the second half by October 31. If the first half is late, interest starts running. A payment postmarked by the due date counts as on time.

faqs.q: Do I owe the real estate excise tax when I sell in Richland?
faqs.a: Usually yes. The seller normally pays it, due on the date of sale to the county treasurer. A completed affidavit must accompany the deed in Benton County.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Richland house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. You can sell as-is, but answer the state disclosure form honestly about roof leaks, structural defects, water and sewer systems and permits. A buyer who purchases as-is will adjust the offer for the condition.

faqs.q: Where do I ask about a senior property tax exemption in Richland?
faqs.a: Ask the Benton County Assessor, who administers the senior and disabled exemptions and deferral programs. The Treasurer's office cannot change the amount due until the Assessor approves the application, so keep paying the bill by its due dates.
